insights.concise_text: The IG-based Attribution method is evaluated by BLEU decrease under perturbations and consistently outperforms Content, Frequency, Attention, and Random across three perturbations.

triple.subject: IG (Attribution)
triple.object: Content, Frequency, Attention, and Random under three perturbations

insights.concise_text: Because Attention simulates SOCRAT and Attribution beats Attention by around 1.0+ BLEU, the gradient-based approach empirically supports its claimed superiority over the best black-box method.

triple.subject: Attribution method
triple.object: the best black-box method SOCRAT

insights.concise_text: The white-box Attribution method uses intermediate gradients, while black-box methods lack model knowledge, explaining the reported superiority of gradient-based word importance estimation.

triple.subject: white-box Attribution method
triple.object: black-box methods without model knowledge

insights.concise_text: Under Mask perturbation with five operations, Attribution reduces BLEU to around half the original score across English⇒French, English⇒Japanese, and reverse directions using Transformer.

triple.subject: Attribution method under Mask perturbation with five operations
triple.object: around half of the original BLEU score across language pairs

insights.concise_text: The RNN-Search validation shows Attribution still outperforms Attention and Random, while RNN-Search is less robust than Transformer with 64% versus 55% BLEU decrease.

triple.subject: Attribution method on RNN-Search
triple.object: Attention method and Random method

insights.concise_text: Attribution is fully unsupervised and does not require external resources, whereas Erasure requires ground-truth references and becomes computation infeasible for multiple-word erasures.

triple.subject: Attribution method
triple.object: Erasure method by avoiding ground-truth references and multiple-word computation infeasibility

insights.concise_text: The word importance computed by IG from contribution matrices is used to detect under-translated words, where Attribution significantly outperforms Erasure and Attention.

triple.subject: IG word importance
triple.object: detecting under-translation errors

insights.concise_text: The finding that nouns matter for Chinese⇒English while prepositions matter for English-French and -Japanese supports the design principle that language characteristics should guide NMT architectures.

triple.subject: language-dependent important syntactic categories
triple.object: essential inductive bias (e.g., language characteristics) for model design

insights.concise_text: Because attention scores weakly correlate with feature importance and Attention only simulates SOCRAT, the paper uses intermediate gradients as the proposed solution for better word importance.

triple.subject: weak correlation of attention scores with feature importance
triple.object: exploiting intermediate gradients to better estimate word importance

insights.concise_text: The experiments use WMT17 Chinese-English, WMT14 English-French, and WAT17 English-Japanese datasets with Transformer and RNN-Search trained for 100k steps.

triple.subject: word importance experiments
triple.object: WMT17 Chinese-English, WMT14 English-French, and WAT17 English-Japanese with Transformer and RNN-Search

insights.concise_text: The decision tree based regression model found POS tags and fertility features contribute over 95%, so following analyses mainly focus on POS tags and fertility properties.

triple.subject: POS tags and fertility features contributing over 95%
triple.object: following analyses to mainly focus on POS tags and fertility properties

insights.concise_text: The hypothesis that a source word corresponding to multiple target words should be more important is confirmed by one-to-many fertility being consistently more important on all three language pairs.

triple.subject: one-to-many fertility being consistently more important on all three language pairs
triple.object: the hypothesis that a source word corresponding to multiple target words should be more important

insights.concise_text: Punctuation is important on English⇒Japanese translation and more important on Japanese⇒English, supporting the conclusion that syntactic distribution with word importance is language-pair related instead of the direction.

triple.subject: punctuation importance on English⇒Japanese translation and Japanese⇒English
triple.object: syntactic distribution with word importance being language-pair related instead of the direction

insights.concise_text: The gradient-based method is superior to several black-box methods in estimating word importance, and detected unimportant words are possibly under-translated.

triple.subject: the gradient-based method
triple.object: detecting possibly under-translated unimportant words

insights.concise_text: Important words are of distinct syntactic categories on different language pairs, supporting the proposal that language-specific inductive bias should be incorporated into the model design.

triple.subject: important words being of distinct syntactic categories on different language pairs
triple.object: incorporating language-specific inductive bias into the model design

insights.concise_text: The gradient-based method bridges the gap between word importance and translation performance, while model interpretability can facilitate model refinement.

triple.subject: the gradient-based method
triple.object: word importance understanding toward model refinement

insights.concise_text: One-to-many fertility is consistently more important on all three language pairs, and reverse directions show one-to-many fertility is more important, further confirming the generality of experimental findings.

triple.subject: one-to-many fertility importance in original and reverse directions
triple.object: the generality of our experimental findings

insights.concise_text: Null-aligned words receive much less attention on three language pairs, and reverse directions show null-aligned fertility is less important, further confirming the generality of experimental findings.

triple.subject: null-aligned fertility being less important in original and reverse directions
triple.object: the generality of our experimental findings
